question: The value of 4cos( {(pi )/(6) - alpha } ) sin( {(pi )/(3) - alpha } ) is equal to:
solution:
Given: 

4cos( {(π )/(6) - alpha } ) sin( {(π )/(3) - alpha } )

Concept used:

Cos (θ - α) = (Cos θ Cosα + Sin θ Sinα)

Sin (θ - α) = (Sinθ Cosα - Cosθ Sinα)

(A + B) (A - B) = A² - B²

Sin²θ + Cos²θ = 1

π = 180° 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5b7101c0b0abb47943f7af05e7717b345d90417692003038950f420fac7962f7.png] 

Calculation:

4cos( {(π )/(6) - α } ) sin( {(π )/(3) - α } )

⇒ 4 × Cos (30° - α) Sin (60° - α)

⇒ 4 × (Cos 30° Cosα + Sin 30° Sinα) × (Sin60° Cosα - Cos60° Sinα)

⇒ 4 × ({sqrt 3} over 2 Cosα + 1 over 2 Sinα) × ({sqrt 3} over 2 Cosα - 1 over 2 Sinα)

⇒ ({sqrt 3} Cosα + Sinα) × ({sqrt 3} Cosα - Sinα)

⇒ ({sqrt 3} Cosα)² - Sin²α

⇒ 3Cos²α - Sin2α

⇒ 3 × (1 - Sin2α) - Sin2α

⇒ 3 - 4sin2α

**∴ The required answer is 3 - 4sin2α.**
